entities.label: Ferdowsi

entities.label: The seven labours of Rostam
entities.summary: The war of Kay Kavus in Mazandaran and Rostam’s journey there through seven trials.

entities.label: Kay Kavus
entities.summary: The king of Iran, proud of his fortune and eager for conquest.

entities.label: The demon minstrel
entities.summary: A demon who comes to the court disguised as a singer from Mazandaran.

entities.label: Tus
entities.summary: A noble of Iran, son of Nowzar.

entities.label: Gudarz
entities.summary: A noble of Iran, son of Keshvad.

entities.label: Giv
entities.summary: A warrior of Iran.

entities.label: Zal
entities.summary: The son of Sam, lord of Nimruz, whose counsel the nobles seek.

facts.text: Lord of Nimruz, father of Rostam

entities.label: Rostam
entities.summary: The son of Zal, a hero of Iran.

entities.label: Iran
entities.summary: The kingdom of Kay Kavus.

entities.label: Mazandaran
entities.summary: A land of demons and sorcerers, praised in song as forever in spring.

entities.label: Sistan
entities.summary: The land of Zal and Rostam, also called Sistan.

entities.label: Milad
entities.summary: A noble to whom Kavus entrusts Iran while he is away.

entities.label: The king of Mazandaran
entities.summary: The ruler of Mazandaran, a sorcerer.

entities.label: Sanjeh
entities.summary: A demon whom the king of Mazandaran sends with a message.

facts.text: Messenger of the king of Mazandaran

entities.label: The White Demon
entities.summary: The mightiest of the demons of Mazandaran, who lives in a cave.

entities.label: Arzhang
entities.summary: A demon commander of Mazandaran.

entities.label: Rudabeh
entities.summary: The mother of Rostam.

entities.label: Mount Asparuz
entities.summary: The mountain at the edge of Mazandaran where Kavus makes camp.

entities.label: Zabulistan
entities.summary: The land of Zal and Rostam.

entities.label: Rakhsh
entities.summary: The horse of Rostam, fierce and watchful.

entities.label: The ram
entities.summary: A wild sheep that appears in the desert.

entities.label: The dragon
entities.summary: A fearsome dragon whose lair lies in the desert.

entities.label: The witch
entities.summary: A sorceress who appears to travellers as a beautiful woman.

entities.label: The field-keeper
entities.summary: The keeper of a green field in Mazandaran.

entities.label: Olad
entities.summary: A young lord of the borderland of Mazandaran.

entities.label: Farhad
entities.summary: A noble of Iran who carries a letter for Kavus.

entities.label: Kalahur
entities.summary: A warrior of Mazandaran known for his fierceness.

entities.label: Juyan
entities.summary: A champion of Mazandaran who challenges the army of Iran.

events.label: The song of Mazandaran
events.summary: Kay Kavus sits on his golden throne among his nobles. A demon, disguised as a minstrel, asks to be let in and sings of Mazandaran: a land of endless spring, flowers, game, brocade and gold.

events.label: Kavus resolves on war
events.summary: Kavus declares that he surpasses Jamshid, Zahhak and Kay Qobad and must lead his army to Mazandaran. The nobles turn pale but dare not object; among themselves Tus, Gudarz and Giv agree to send for Zal, who may turn the king from his plan.

events.label: Zal comes to court
events.summary: A rider reaches Zal in Nimruz with the nobles' message. Zal grieves at the king's recklessness but resolves to go, leaving Rostam behind with the army, and the nobles ride out to meet him.

events.label: Zal's counsel refused
events.summary: Zal warns Kavus that no earlier king dared Mazandaran, a land of demons and spells that neither sword nor treasure can win. Kavus answers that he is greater than those kings and that Zal and Rostam should guard Iran while he goes; Zal bids him farewell, wishing him no regret.

events.label: The march and the sack
events.summary: Kavus leaves Milad in charge of Iran and leads the army to Mount Asparuz. He sends Giv with two thousand men, who fall on the city of Mazandaran, kill and plunder and find it as rich as paradise.

events.label: Darkness falls
events.summary: The king of Mazandaran sends the demon Sanjeh to the White Demon for help. At night the White Demon brings a cloud of pitch and smoke; at daybreak Kavus and most of his army are blind. The demons bind them and give the king's treasure to Arzhang, and the White Demon leaves them to suffer.

events.label: Rostam is sent
events.summary: Kavus sends a rider to Zal, confessing that he ignored his counsel. Zal tells Rostam to saddle Rakhsh: of the two roads, he should take the short one of seven stages, full of demons and lions. Rostam swears to free the king, and Rudabeh weeps as he leaves.

events.label: First labour: the lion
events.summary: Riding day and night, Rostam lassos and roasts an onager and lies down to sleep in a reed bed. A lion comes upon them in the night; Rakhsh strikes it down and tears it apart. Rostam wakes and scolds Rakhsh for fighting alone instead of waking him.

events.label: Second labour: thirst
events.summary: In a burning desert Rostam and Rakhsh are near death from thirst. Rostam prays and falls to the ground; a wild ram passes, and following it he finds a spring. He blesses the ram, bathes, hunts and eats, and before sleeping tells Rakhsh to fight no one but to wake him.

events.label: Third labour: the dragon
events.summary: A dragon comes out in the night. Twice Rakhsh wakes Rostam, and twice the dragon vanishes into the dark, so Rostam threatens to kill his horse. The third time God lets him see it; Rostam names himself, and with Rakhsh biting the dragon's shoulder he cuts off its head.

events.label: Fourth labour: the witch
events.summary: Rostam finds by a spring a feast laid out with wine and a lute, and sings of his own hard life. A witch, adorned as a beautiful woman, comes to sit with him; when he names God as he hands her wine, her face darkens. He catches her with his lasso, she turns into a wrinkled hag, and he cuts her in two.

entityAssociations.role: traveller who sees through the spell

events.label: The field-keeper's ears
events.summary: Rostam rides through a land of total darkness into green fields, lets Rakhsh graze in a crop and sleeps. The field-keeper strikes his foot and scolds him; Rostam tears off both his ears without a word, and the man runs to his lord Olad.

events.label: Fifth labour: Olad
events.summary: Olad rides out with his men; Rostam scatters them and lassos Olad. He promises to make him king of Mazandaran if he shows him truly where the White Demon lives and where Kavus is held. Olad describes the long and terrible road and the armies of the demons, and Rostam laughs.

events.label: The fires of Mazandaran
events.summary: Riding day and night they reach Mount Asparuz, where Kavus was struck down. At midnight they see fires burning: Olad says it is the city of Mazandaran, where Arzhang the demon keeps watch. At dawn Rostam ties Olad to a tree and rides on.

events.label: Sixth labour: Arzhang
events.summary: Rostam rides into the camp of Arzhang and roars; when the demon comes out, Rostam seizes him by the head and ears, tears off his head and throws it among the demons, who flee in terror.

events.label: Rostam reaches the king
events.summary: Guided by Olad, Rostam enters the city where Kavus is held. The blind king recognises the neigh of Rakhsh and rejoices. He embraces Rostam and tells him to hurry to the cave of the White Demon beyond seven mountains: only three drops of the demon's blood can restore the sight of the king and his men.

events.label: Seventh labour: the White Demon
events.summary: Olad advises waiting until the heat of noon, when the demons sleep. Rostam then cuts through the guards and enters the dark cave, where the White Demon rises like a black mountain. Rostam cuts off a leg; they wrestle until the ground is mud with blood, and at last Rostam lifts him, dashes him down, stabs him and tears out his liver.

entityAssociations.role: hero who kills the White Demon

events.label: Olad's reward promised
events.summary: Olad reminds Rostam of his promise. Rostam answers that he will give him all Mazandaran, but first the king of Mazandaran must be thrown from his throne.

events.label: Sight restored
events.summary: The demon's blood is dropped into the king's eyes and he sees again. Kavus sits on the throne of Mazandaran with Rostam and his nobles and feasts for a week; then his army burns the city, until he commands the killing to stop and sends a messenger to the king of Mazandaran.

events.label: Farhad's letter
events.summary: Kavus writes to the king of Mazandaran to come and submit, or share the fate of Arzhang and the White Demon. Farhad carries the letter; the king's men try to crush his hand, but he does not flinch. Reading of the White Demon's death, the king weeps with rage.

events.label: A defiant answer
events.summary: The king of Mazandaran answers that his army and his elephants are greater than Iran's and that he will bring war upon it. Kavus is ashamed, and Rostam offers to carry the next message himself.

events.label: Rostam as envoy
events.summary: On the road Rostam uproots a tree and hurls it at the riders sent to meet him. A warrior crushes his hand in greeting, and Rostam laughs and crushes back; the fierce Kalahur tries the same and his nails fall out, and he urges his king to make peace. The king scorns Kavus's letter; Rostam refuses his gifts and returns with the news.

events.label: The armies meet
events.summary: Both kings march out. Kavus sets Tus on the right, Gudarz on the left, himself in the centre and Rostam at the front. Juyan, a champion of Mazandaran, rides out and challenges Iran; no one answers until Rostam asks leave, runs him through, lifts him from the saddle like a bird on a spit and throws him down.

events.label: A week of battle
events.summary: The two armies fight for a week. On the eighth day Kavus takes off his crown, weeps before God and prays for victory; then the whole army attacks, with Rostam in the centre and Giv, Gudarz, Tus and the other heroes around him, until blood runs in streams.

events.label: The king turned to stone
events.summary: Rostam charges the king of Mazandaran and strikes his belt with a spear, but the king turns by sorcery into a rock. No one else can move it; Rostam lifts it alone and carries it to Kavus's tent, threatening to break it apart. The king emerges, and Kavus, finding him unworthy of the throne, has him put to death.

events.label: Olad made king
events.summary: Kavus divides the spoils, prays for a week and gives to the needy. Rostam tells him that his victory owes much to Olad, who showed him every road, and asks for him to be made ruler of Mazandaran; Kavus grants it and leaves for Iran.

events.label: Home to Iran
events.summary: Iran welcomes Kavus with music and joy. He gives Rostam a throne, a crown, servants, horses and gold, and a charter over all of Nimruz. Rostam returns home; Kavus makes Tus commander of the army and gives Isfahan to Gudarz, and rules in justice and plenty.
